newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares sag but close above 4,100 SMI points.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares sag but close above 4,100 SMI points.

text.p: Swiss shares ended one percent lower on Friday on the back of a Wall Street slump on Thursday but the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) managed to close above 4,100 points after temporarily falling below that level.
Dealers said a correction had been expected.

"The reaction is normal after the market has long been overbought," one trader said, adding that prospects for further gains remained good. "I have the feeling there won't be any U.S. interest rate hike anytime soon", he said.
But another trader said the possibility of higher U.S. interest rates may continue to weigh on the market.
The SMI fell 35.5 points, or 0.85 percent, to 4,125.5. On Thursday, the SMI closed at a record for the third day in a row at 4,161.0 points. Friday's low was 4,082.7.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 20.62 points, or 0.78 percent, to 2,639.47
The highflyers of the past few days were under heavy pressure.

Roche certificates, which had hit an all-time high of 12,500 francs on Wednesday, slumped 200 francs or 1.67 percent to 11,780. The mid-week jump had been triggered by rumours that Roche may plan a merger or a divestment.
Thursday's prominent winner UBS also gave up ground. The bearer shares lost nine francs to 1,180.
